optimized_sql:
SELECT
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip,
    SUM(rs."30 days") AS "30 days",
    SUM(rs."31-60 days") AS "31-60 days",
    SUM(rs."61-90 days") AS "61-90 days",
    SUM(rs."91-120 days") AS "91-120 days",
    SUM(rs.">120 days") AS ">120 days"
FROM (
    SELECT
        jr.ss_store_sk,
        CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN jr.day_diff <= 30 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS integer) AS "30 days",
        CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN jr.day_diff > 30 AND jr.day_diff <= 60 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS integer) AS "31-60 days",
        CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN jr.day_diff > 60 AND jr.day_diff <= 90 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS integer) AS "61-90 days",
        CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN jr.day_diff > 90 AND jr.day_diff <= 120 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS integer) AS "91-120 days",
        CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN jr.day_diff > 120 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS integer) AS ">120 days"
    FROM (
        SELECT
            ss.ss_store_sk,
            (sr.sr_returned_date_sk - ss.ss_sold_date_sk) AS day_diff
        FROM date_dim d2
        JOIN store_returns sr ON sr.sr_returned_date_sk = d2.d_date_sk
        JOIN store_sales ss ON ss.ss_item_sk = sr.sr_item_sk
                           AND ss.ss_ticket_number = sr.sr_ticket_number
                           AND ss.ss_customer_sk = sr.sr_customer_sk
        WHERE d2.d_year = 2001
          AND d2.d_moy = 8
          AND ss.ss_sold_date_sk IS NOT NULL
    ) AS jr
    GROUP BY jr.ss_store_sk
) AS rs
JOIN store s ON s.s_store_sk = rs.ss_store_sk
GROUP BY
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip
ORDER BY
    s.s_store_name,
    s.s_company_id,
    s.s_street_number,
    s.s_street_name,
    s.s_street_type,
    s.s_suite_number,
    s.s_city,
    s.s_county,
    s.s_state,
    s.s_zip
LIMIT 100

reasoning_trace:
1. JOIN REORDER / FILTER PUSH-DOWN — TARGET: date_dim d2 → store_returns (sr_returned_date_sk) → store_sales (ss_item_sk, ss_ticket_number) — TRANSFORMATION: Start from the filtered d2 rows (d_year=2001, d_moy=8), join store_returns on sr_returned_date_sk, then probe store_sales by its primary key (ss_item_sk, ss_ticket_number), avoiding a full scan/join of the 57.6M-row store_sales table.

2. ELIMINATE UNUSED DIMENSION JOIN — TARGET: date_dim d1 / ss_sold_date_sk = d1.d_date_sk — TRANSFORMATION: Remove the join to d1 because it supplies no predicate or output columns; if the original inner-join null-removal semantics must be preserved exactly, replace it with `ss_sold_date_sk IS NOT NULL` (the FK guarantees the join is otherwise a no-op).

3. COVERING INDEX — TARGET: store_returns(sr_returned_date_sk, sr_item_sk, sr_ticket_number, sr_customer_sk) — TRANSFORMATION: Create a covering index with sr_returned_date_sk leading so the August-2001 return rows are obtained by an index-only scan and the join keys to store_sales are already available without scanning the 5.75M-row store_returns heap.

4. PUSH-DOWN AGGREGATION — TARGET: final GROUP BY after the store_sales–store_returns join — TRANSFORMATION: In a derived table, compute the five bucket sums grouped only by ss_store_sk, then join to store and apply the existing GROUP BY/ORDER BY on the resulting at-most-44-row set instead of grouping the full joined row set.

5. REUSE DATE-DIFFERENCE EXPRESSION — TARGET: repeated `(sr_returned_date_sk - ss_sold_date_sk)` in the five CASE expressions — TRANSFORMATION: Compute the sale-to-return day difference once per joined row in the derived table and reuse that single value in all five bucket CASE expressions, preserving the same bucket boundaries.
